async def test_query_osv_parses_vulnerabilities():

def _release_context(changes: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Fetch bounded upstream release notes when an updated package points to GitHub."""
    results: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    candidates = [item for item in changes if item.get("head_version") not in {"", "removed", "not present"}][:5]
    try:
        client = httpx.Client(timeout=8.0, headers={"Accept": "application/vnd.github+json"})
    except Exception as exc:
        return [{"package": item.get("package", "unknown package"), "version": item.get("head_version", ""),
                 "status": "lookup_failed", "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"[:500],
                 "release_notes": "", "migration_links": []} for item in candidates]
    try:
        for change in candidates:
            ecosystem, name, version = change["ecosystem"], change["package"], change["head_version"]
            registry_url = (
                f"https://pypi.org/pypi/{name}/{version}/json" if ecosystem == "pypi"
                else f"https://registry.npmjs.org/{name}/{version}" if ecosystem == "npm"
                else ""
            )
            if not registry_url:
                results.append({"package": name, "version": version, "status": "not_applicable",
                                "release_notes": "", "migration_links": []})
                continue
            try:
                registry = client.get(registry_url)
                registry.raise_for_status()
                data = registry.json()
                info = data.get("info", {}) if ecosystem == "pypi" else data
                project_urls = info.get("project_urls", {}) if ecosystem == "pypi" else {}
                migration_links = []
                if isinstance(project_urls, dict):
                    migration_links = [
                        {"label": str(label), "url": str(url)}
                        for label, url in project_urls.items()
                        if re.search(r"change|release|migration|documentation|docs", str(label), re.I)
                        and str(url).startswith("https://")
                    ][:8]
                repository_url = str(
                    project_urls.get("Source", project_urls.get("Repository", project_urls.get("Homepage", "")))
                    if isinstance(project_urls, dict) else ""
                )
                if ecosystem == "npm":
                    repository_data = data.get("repository", {})
                    repository_url = repository_data.get("url", "") if isinstance(repository_data, dict) else str(repository_data)
                    homepage = str(data.get("homepage", ""))
                    if homepage.startswith("https://"):
                        migration_links.append({"label": "package homepage", "url": homepage})
                match = re.search(r"github\.com[:/]([^/]+)/([^/#.]+)", str(repository_url))
                if not match:
                    results.append({"package": name, "version": version,
                                    "status": "source_unavailable", "release_notes": "",
                                    "migration_links": migration_links})
                    continue
                owner, repo = match.groups()
                note = ""
                release_found = False
                for tag in (f"v{version}", version):
                    release = client.get(f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/tags/{tag}")
                    if release.status_code == 404:
                        continue
                    release.raise_for_status()
                    release_found = True
                    note = str(release.json().get("body", ""))[:3_000]
                    break
                results.append({"package": name, "version": version,
                                "status": "retrieved" if note else "no_release_notes",
                                "release_found": release_found,
                                "release_notes": note, "migration_links": migration_links})
            except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
                results.append({"package": name, "version": version,
                                "status": "lookup_failed", "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"[:500],
                                "release_notes": "", "migration_links": []})
    finally:
        client.close()
    return results

def review_dependabot_pull_request(
    repository: str | Path,
    pull_request: str,
    *,
    github_client: Any | None = None,
    osv_client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
    usage_analyzer: Callable[[Path, list[dict[str, Any]]], list[dict[str, Any]]] | None = None,
    release_context_lookup: Callable[[list[dict[str, Any]]], list[dict[str, Any]]] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compare base and Dependabot head without changing or pushing either ref.

    Tests run through the existing environment-stripped runner. GitHub API
    credentials are used only to read PR metadata and are never passed to tests.
    """
    root = Path(repository).expanduser().resolve()
    if not root.is_dir() or not (root / ".git").exists():
        raise ValueError(f"Not a Git working tree: {root}")
    requested_repo, number = parse_pull_request_reference(pull_request)
    origin_repo = _github_origin(root)
    if requested_repo and requested_repo.casefold() != origin_repo.casefold():
        raise ValueError(f"PR belongs to {requested_repo}, but repository origin is {origin_repo}")

    owns_client = github_client is None
    if github_client is None:
        headers = {"Accept": "application/vnd.github+json", "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28"}
        if os.getenv("GITHUB_TOKEN"):
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {os.environ['GITHUB_TOKEN']}"
        github_client = httpx.Client(headers=headers, timeout=30)
    metadata_url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{origin_repo}/pulls/{number}"
    try:
        response = github_client.get(metadata_url)
        response.raise_for_status()
        metadata = response.json()
        # A PR can retain an older base SHA after the target branch advances.
        # Accept that only when the reported base is an ancestor of the fetched
        # target branch. We then test a local merge of the PR head onto today's
        # base, which represents the code GitHub would merge. Head SHA must still
        # match exactly; unrelated or rewritten base history is rejected.
        ref_mismatch: dict[str, str] = {}
        base_advanced = False
        review_base_sha = ""
        for snapshot_attempt in range(3):
            if metadata.get("state") != "open":
                raise ValueError("This Dependabot review path currently accepts open pull requests only")
            if str(metadata.get("user", {}).get("login", "")).casefold() != "dependabot[bot]":
                raise ValueError("The selected pull request was not opened by dependabot[bot]")
            base_branch = str(metadata.get("base", {}).get("ref", ""))
            head_branch = str(metadata.get("head", {}).get("ref", ""))
            base_sha = str(metadata.get("base", {}).get("sha", ""))
            head_sha = str(metadata.get("head", {}).get("sha", ""))
            if not all((base_branch, head_branch, base_sha, head_sha)):
                raise ValueError("GitHub did not return complete base/head branch metadata")

            base_ref = f"refs/agent-review/{number}/base"
            head_ref = f"refs/agent-review/{number}/head"
            _git(root, "fetch", "--no-tags", "origin",
                 f"+refs/heads/{base_branch}:{base_ref}",
                 f"+refs/pull/{number}/head:{head_ref}")
            fetched_base = _git(root, "rev-parse", base_ref)
            fetched_head = _git(root, "rev-parse", head_ref)
            if fetched_head == head_sha:
                if fetched_base == base_sha:
                    review_base_sha = base_sha
                    break
                # This is a safe forward movement only when the PR's recorded
                # base commit is still in the current target branch history.
                merge_base = _git(root, "merge-base", base_sha, fetched_base)
                if merge_base == base_sha:
                    review_base_sha = fetched_base
                    base_advanced = True
                    break

            ref_mismatch = {
                "expected_base_sha": base_sha,
                "fetched_base_sha": fetched_base,
                "expected_head_sha": head_sha,
                "fetched_head_sha": fetched_head,
            }
            for ref in (base_ref, head_ref):
                subprocess.run(["git", "update-ref", "-d", ref], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
            if snapshot_attempt < 2:
                response = github_client.get(metadata_url)
                response.raise_for_status()
                metadata = response.json()
        else:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "GitHub PR refs did not stabilize after 3 attempts; refusing to review a mismatched snapshot. "
                f"Last comparison: {ref_mismatch}"
            )

def upgrade_guidance_for_finding(finding: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Summarize OSV's earliest declared fixed version for the current package."""
    package = finding.get("package", {})
    versions = fixed_versions_for_finding(finding, package)
    return {
        "source": "OSV affected range events",
        "current_version": str(package.get("version", "")),
        "recommended_version": versions[0] if versions else "",
        "fixed_versions": versions,
        "status": "candidate_available" if versions else "no_orderable_fixed_version",
        "note": (
            "Use the earliest OSV fixed version newer than the detected version; "
            "compatibility must still be checked by tests and a post-patch OSV scan."
            if versions else
            "OSV did not provide an orderable fixed version for this package and advisory; do not guess an upgrade."
        ),
    }

def _scan(repository: Path, client: httpx.AsyncClient | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    packages, manifests = _read_packages(repository)
    resolved = [package for package in packages if package.get("version")]
    unresolved = [package["name"] for package in packages if not package.get("version")]
    scan_error = ""
    try:
        findings = run_async(scan_packages(resolved, client)) if resolved else []
    except Exception as exc:
        # Keep the resolved inventory so changed packages remain identifiable,
        # while making the failed advisory lookup explicit to classification.
        findings = []
        scan_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
    roots, edges = _dependency_index(repository)
    manifest_map = _package_manifest_map(repository)
    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    seen: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    for item in findings:
        package = item.get("package", {})
        ecosystem = str(package.get("ecosystem", ""))
        name = str(package.get("name", ""))
        normalized_name = re.sub(r"[-_.]+", "-", name.casefold()) if ecosystem.casefold() == "pypi" else name.casefold()
        advisory_id = str(item.get("id", "unknown"))
        identity = (ecosystem.casefold(), normalized_name, advisory_id.casefold())
        if identity in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(identity)
        dependency_key = (ecosystem.casefold(), normalized_name)
        paths = _dependency_paths(roots, edges, dependency_key)
        relationship = "direct" if dependency_key in roots else ("transitive" if paths else "unknown")
        matching_affected = [
            affected for affected in item.get("affected", [])
            if str(affected.get("package", {}).get("ecosystem", "")).casefold() == ecosystem.casefold()
            and (re.sub(r"[-_.]+", "-", str(affected.get("package", {}).get("name", "")).casefold())
                 if ecosystem.casefold() == "pypi" else str(affected.get("package", {}).get("name", "")).casefold()) == normalized_name
        ]
        affected_ranges = [
            {key: value for key, value in version_range.items() if key in {"type", "repo", "events"}}
            for affected in matching_affected for version_range in affected.get("ranges", [])
            if isinstance(version_range, dict)
        ]
        affected_versions = sorted({str(version) for affected in matching_affected for version in affected.get("versions", [])})
        fixed_versions = sorted({str(event["fixed"]) for version_range in affected_ranges
                                 for event in version_range.get("events", [])
                                 if str(version_range.get("type", "")).upper() in {"ECOSYSTEM", "SEMVER"}
                                 and isinstance(event, dict) and event.get("fixed")})
        severity = [
            {key: str(value) for key, value in entry.items() if key in {"type", "score"} and value is not None}
            for entry in item.get("severity", []) if isinstance(entry, dict)
        ]
        records.append({
            "finding_identity": f"{ecosystem.casefold()}:{normalized_name}:{advisory_id.casefold()}",
            "id": advisory_id,
            "package": name,
            "ecosystem": ecosystem,
            "version": str(package.get("version", "")),
            "installed_version": str(package.get("version", "")) or None,
            "summary": str(item.get("summary", "")),
            "severity": severity,
            "severity_status": "available" if severity else "unavailable",
            "affected_ranges": affected_ranges,
            "affected_versions": affected_versions,
            "affected_range_status": "available" if affected_ranges or affected_versions else "unavailable",
            "version_assessment": assess_version_affected_by_advisory(item, str(package.get("version", ""))),
            "fixed_versions": fixed_versions,
            "fixed_version_status": "available" if fixed_versions else "unavailable",
            "manifest_files": manifest_map.get(dependency_key, []),
            "relationship": relationship,
            "dependency_paths": paths,
            "dependency_path_status": "available" if paths else "unavailable",
            "aliases": sorted({str(alias) for alias in item.get("aliases", []) if alias})[:20],
            "references": [
                {key: str(ref[key]) for key in ("type", "url") if ref.get(key)}
                for ref in item.get("references", [])[:10] if isinstance(ref, dict)
            ],
        })
    return {
        "scan_status": "failed" if scan_error else "complete",
        **({"scan_error": scan_error} if scan_error else {}),
        "manifests": manifests,
        "packages_checked": len(resolved),
        "unresolved_packages": unresolved,
        "findings": records,
        "resolved_packages": resolved,
    }

def parse_package_json(content: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Parse direct npm dependencies, treating only exact versions as resolved."""
    import json
    data = json.loads(content)
    result: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for section in ("dependencies", "devDependencies", "optionalDependencies", "peerDependencies"):
        for name, version in (data.get(section) or {}).items():
            version_text = str(version).strip()
            # Semver ranges (including ^, ~, >=, tags and workspace specs)
            # are not the installed version. A lockfile parser supplies that.
            exact = re.fullmatch(r"(?:=|v)?(\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?(?:\+[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?)", version_text)
            clean_version = exact.group(1) if exact else ""
            result.append({"name": name, "version": clean_version, "ecosystem": "npm"})
    return result

def build_graph(
    mcp: MCPClient | None = None,
    *,
    model: Any | None = None,
    http_client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
    github_client: Any | None = None,
    checkpointer: Any | None = None,

    run_id: str | None = None,
    interrupt_before_pr: bool = False,
) -> Any:
    """Build a workflow with injectable services for tests and local runs."""
    deps = create_dependencies(
        mcp, model=model, http_client=http_client, github_client=github_client,
        audit_database_path=audit_database_path, run_id=run_id or uuid.uuid4().hex,
    )
    scan_node = partial(node_scan_vulnerabilities, deps=deps)
    nodes = {
        "scan": scan_node,
        "select_finding": partial(node_select_finding, deps=deps),
        "report_source_usage": partial(node_report_source_usage, deps=deps),
        "prepare_worktree": partial(node_prepare_worktree, deps=deps),
        "baseline_tests": partial(node_run_baseline_tests, deps=deps),
        "investigate": partial(node_investigate_and_plan, deps=deps),
        "apply": partial(node_apply_patch, deps=deps),
        "regenerate_lockfile": partial(node_regenerate_lockfile, deps=deps),
        "tests": partial(node_run_tests, deps=deps),
        "verify_patch": partial(node_verify_patch, scan_node=scan_node),
        "await_approval": partial(node_await_approval, deps=deps),
        "create_pr": partial(node_create_pull_request, deps=deps),
        "record_failure": partial(node_record_failure, deps=deps),
        "cleanup_worktree": partial(node_cleanup_worktree, deps=deps),
        "finalize": partial(node_finalize_batch, deps=deps),
        "log_failure": partial(node_log_failure, deps=deps),
    }
    nodes["rescan"] = partial(
        node_rescan_after_pr, deps=deps, scan_node=nodes["scan"],
    )

    graph = StateGraph(State)
    for name, node in nodes.items():
        stage = {
            "investigate": "planning", "apply": "patch",
            "regenerate_lockfile": "lockfile",
            "verify_patch": "verification", "await_approval": "approval",
            "create_pr": "pull_request", "cleanup_worktree": "cleanup",

def test_cli_accepts_artifact_url_for_matching_repository_report(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    evidence_path = tmp_path / "evidence.json"
    artifact_url = "https://github.com/acme/demo/actions/runs/10/artifacts/20"
    evidence_path.write_text(json.dumps({
        "schema_version": 2,
        "mode": "dependabot_pr_review",
        "status": "review_complete",
        "repository_full_name": "acme/demo",
        "pull_request": {"number": 17, "author": "dependabot[bot]", "head_sha": "abc123"},
    }))
    archived = tmp_path / "saved report"

    class FakeReviewGraph:
        def invoke(self, state):
            assert state["report"]["report_artifact_url"] == artifact_url
            return {"report": {**state["report"], "ai_review": "Short review", "ai_review_status": "complete"}}

    monkeypatch.setattr(main, "build_dependabot_review_graph", lambda **_kwargs: FakeReviewGraph())
    monkeypatch.setattr(main, "DEFAULT_REPORT_DIRECTORY", archived)

    code = main.main([
        "--analyze-report", str(evidence_path),
        "--report-artifact-url", artifact_url,
    ])

    files = list(archived.glob("review-*.json"))
    assert code == 0
    assert len(files) == 1
    assert json.loads(files[0].read_text())["report_artifact_url"] == artifact_url
    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out)["status"] == "review_complete"

class DependabotReviewState(TypedDict, total=False):
    repository: str
    pull_request: str
    report: dict[str, Any]

def _tree_sitter_chunks(
    relative_path: str, source: str, parser_cache_dir: str | Path | None = None,
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Extract JS/TS declarations with Tree-sitter when available."""
    try:
        from tree_sitter_language_pack import PackConfig, configure, get_parser

        cache_dir = Path(parser_cache_dir or (Path.home() / ".vulnerability-patch-agent" / "code-index" / "tree-sitter"))
        cache_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
        configure(PackConfig(cache_dir=str(cache_dir)))

        language = CODE_SUFFIX_LANGUAGE[Path(relative_path).suffix.lower()]
        parser = get_parser(language)
        tree = parser.parse(source.encode("utf-8"))
    except Exception:
        return []
    lines = source.splitlines()
    declaration_types = {
        "function_declaration", "function_expression", "generator_function_declaration",
        "method_definition", "class_declaration", "class", "lexical_declaration",
    }
    chunks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    def visit(node: Any, parent_symbol: str = "") -> None:
        if node.type in declaration_types:
            start, end = int(node.start_point.row) + 1, int(node.end_point.row) + 1
            text = "\n".join(lines[start - 1:end])
            name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")
            name = source[name_node.start_byte:name_node.end_byte] if name_node else node.type
            symbol = f"{parent_symbol}.{name}" if parent_symbol else name
            if len(text) <= MAX_CHUNK_CHARS:
                chunks.append({
                    "path": relative_path, "symbol": symbol,
                    "line_start": start, "line_end": end,
                    "language": CODE_SUFFIX_LANGUAGE[Path(relative_path).suffix.lower()],
                    "content": text,
                })
                # For a declaration, only recurse into nested declarations so
                # methods are independently retrievable without indexing every
                # expression as a separate chunk.
                for child in node.children:
                    visit(child, symbol if node.type in {"class", "class_declaration"} else parent_symbol)
                return
        for child in node.children:
            visit(child, parent_symbol)

    visit(tree.root_node)
    return chunks

def _javascript_fallback_chunks(relative_path: str, source: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Preserve common JS/TS declaration boundaries if a grammar is unavailable."""
    lines = source.splitlines()
    declaration = re.compile(
        r"^\s*(?:export\s+)?(?:default\s+)?(?:async\s+)?"
        r"(?:function\s*\*?\s*([\w$]+)|class\s+([\w$]+)|"
        r"(?:const|let|var)\s+([\w$]+)\s*=\s*(?:async\s*)?(?:\([^)]*\)|[\w$]+)\s*=>)"
    )
    chunks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        match = declaration.match(line)
        if not match:
            continue
        name = next((value for value in match.groups() if value), "anonymous")
        brace_balance = 0
        saw_brace = False
        end_index = index
        for end_index in range(index, min(len(lines), index + 120)):
            brace_balance += lines[end_index].count("{") - lines[end_index].count("}")
            saw_brace = saw_brace or "{" in lines[end_index]
            if saw_brace and brace_balance <= 0:
                break
        text = "\n".join(lines[index:end_index + 1])
        chunks.append({
            "path": relative_path, "symbol": name,
            "line_start": index + 1, "line_end": end_index + 1,
            "language": CODE_SUFFIX_LANGUAGE[Path(relative_path).suffix.lower()],
            "content": text,
        })
    return chunks

async def test_query_osv_parses_vulnerabilities():

    # only AsyncClient.post() is awaited.

    response.raise_for_status.return_value = None

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_scan_packages_attaches_package_to_vulnerability():
    response = Mock()
    response.json.return_value = {"vulns": [{"id": "OSV-1"}]}
    client = AsyncMock()
    client.post.return_value = response
    findings = await scan_packages([{"name": "demo", "version": "1.0", "ecosystem": "PyPI"}], client)
    assert findings == [{"id": "OSV-1", "package": {"name": "demo", "version": "1.0", "ecosystem": "PyPI"}}]

async def scan_packages(
    packages: list[dict[str, str]],
    client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
    *,
    max_concurrency: int = 8,
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Query OSV concurrently with a small bound, preserving package order.

    OSV calls are independent, so bounded concurrency reduces scan latency
    without creating an unbounded burst against the public API. ``gather``
    preserves input ordering, which keeps report and branch ordering stable.
    """
    if max_concurrency < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_concurrency must be at least 1")
    semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)

    async def scan_one(package: dict[str, str]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        async with semaphore:
            findings = await query_osv(package, client)
            return [{**vulnerability, "package": package} for vulnerability in findings]

    groups = await asyncio.gather(*(scan_one(package) for package in packages))
    return [finding for group in groups for finding in group]

def review_dependabot_pull_request(
    repository: str | Path,
    pull_request: str,
    *,
    github_client: Any | None = None,
    osv_client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
    usage_analyzer: Callable[[Path, list[dict[str, Any]]], list[dict[str, Any]]] | None = None,
    release_context_lookup: Callable[[list[dict[str, Any]]], list[dict[str, Any]]] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compare base and Dependabot head without changing or pushing either ref.

    Tests run through the existing environment-stripped runner. GitHub API
    credentials are used only to read PR metadata and are never passed to tests.
    """
    root = Path(repository).expanduser().resolve()
    if not root.is_dir() or not (root / ".git").exists():
        raise ValueError(f"Not a Git working tree: {root}")
    requested_repo, number = parse_pull_request_reference(pull_request)
    origin_repo = _github_origin(root)
    if requested_repo and requested_repo.casefold() != origin_repo.casefold():
        raise ValueError(f"PR belongs to {requested_repo}, but repository origin is {origin_repo}")

    owns_client = github_client is None
    if github_client is None:
        headers = {"Accept": "application/vnd.github+json", "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28"}
        if os.getenv("GITHUB_TOKEN"):
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {os.environ['GITHUB_TOKEN']}"
        github_client = httpx.Client(headers=headers, timeout=30)
    metadata_url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{origin_repo}/pulls/{number}"
    try:
        response = github_client.get(metadata_url)
        response.raise_for_status()
        metadata = response.json()
        # A PR can retain an older base SHA after the target branch advances.
        # Accept that only when the reported base is an ancestor of the fetched
        # target branch. We then test a local merge of the PR head onto today's
        # base, which represents the code GitHub would merge. Head SHA must still
        # match exactly; unrelated or rewritten base history is rejected.
        ref_mismatch: dict[str, str] = {}
        base_advanced = False
        review_base_sha = ""
        for snapshot_attempt in range(3):
            if metadata.get("state") != "open":
                raise ValueError("This Dependabot review path currently accepts open pull requests only")
            if str(metadata.get("user", {}).get("login", "")).casefold() != "dependabot[bot]":
                raise ValueError("The selected pull request was not opened by dependabot[bot]")
            base_branch = str(metadata.get("base", {}).get("ref", ""))
            head_branch = str(metadata.get("head", {}).get("ref", ""))
            base_sha = str(metadata.get("base", {}).get("sha", ""))
            head_sha = str(metadata.get("head", {}).get("sha", ""))
            if not all((base_branch, head_branch, base_sha, head_sha)):
                raise ValueError("GitHub did not return complete base/head branch metadata")

            base_ref = f"refs/agent-review/{number}/base"
            head_ref = f"refs/agent-review/{number}/head"
            _git(root, "fetch", "--no-tags", "origin",
                 f"+refs/heads/{base_branch}:{base_ref}",
                 f"+refs/pull/{number}/head:{head_ref}")
            fetched_base = _git(root, "rev-parse", base_ref)
            fetched_head = _git(root, "rev-parse", head_ref)
            if fetched_head == head_sha:
                if fetched_base == base_sha:
                    review_base_sha = base_sha
                    break
                # This is a safe forward movement only when the PR's recorded
                # base commit is still in the current target branch history.
                merge_base = _git(root, "merge-base", base_sha, fetched_base)
                if merge_base == base_sha:
                    review_base_sha = fetched_base
                    base_advanced = True
                    break

            ref_mismatch = {
                "expected_base_sha": base_sha,
                "fetched_base_sha": fetched_base,
                "expected_head_sha": head_sha,
                "fetched_head_sha": fetched_head,
            }
            for ref in (base_ref, head_ref):
                subprocess.run(["git", "update-ref", "-d", ref], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
            if snapshot_attempt < 2:
                response = github_client.get(metadata_url)
                response.raise_for_status()
                metadata = response.json()
        else:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "GitHub PR refs did not stabilize after 3 attempts; refusing to review a mismatched snapshot. "
                f"Last comparison: {ref_mismatch}"
            )

def test_secure_runner_strips_secrets(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", "/usr/bin")
    monkeypatch.setenv("HOME", str(tmp_path))
    monkeypatch.setenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "openai-secret-value")
    monkeypatch.setenv("GITHUB_TOKEN", "github-secret-value")
    monkeypatch.setenv("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "aws-access-secret")
    monkeypatch.setenv("AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "aws-secret-value")
    monkeypatch.setenv("SSH_AUTH_SOCK", "/tmp/ssh-agent.sock")
    monkeypatch.setenv("SSH_PRIVATE_KEY", "ssh-private-secret")
    captured = {}

    def fake_run(command, **kwargs):
        captured["command"] = command
        captured["env"] = kwargs["env"]
        captured["timeout"] = kwargs["timeout"]
        return CompletedProcess(command, 0, stdout="ok", stderr="")

    monkeypatch.setattr(sandbox_runner.subprocess, "run", fake_run)
    result = sandbox_runner.run_tests_safely(str(tmp_path), ["pytest", "-q"])

    assert result["passed"] is True
    assert captured["timeout"] == 60
    assert captured["env"]["PATH"] == "/usr/bin"
    assert captured["env"]["HOME"] == str(tmp_path)
    assert captured["env"]["CI"] == "true"
    assert not any(key.startswith(("AWS_", "SSH_")) for key in captured["env"])
    assert "OPENAI_API_KEY" not in captured["env"]
    assert "GITHUB_TOKEN" not in captured["env"]

metric_definitions.configuration_only_cases: Validated against the named config file separately; not part of source-retrieval metrics because config files are not indexed.
metric_definitions.macro_averaging: Aggregate scores are arithmetic means of eligible per-case scores; recall and MRR average positive source-evidence cases only.
metric_definitions.no_evidence_false_positive_results: Retrieved source results for eligible cases with no labelled source evidence; configuration-only cases are excluded.
metric_definitions.non_relevant_results_at_5: For positive source-evidence cases, retrieved source results not matching any labelled relevant location.
metric_definitions.precision_at_5: Relevant retrieved source locations divided by 5; unfilled result slots count as non-relevant.
metric_definitions.recall_at_5: Distinct labelled relevant source locations present in top 5 divided by total labelled locations; negative, configuration-only, and uncertain cases excluded.
metric_definitions.reciprocal_rank: Reciprocal rank of the first relevant source location; averaged only across positive, non-uncertain source cases.
metric_definitions.uncertain_cases: Reported with per-case raw results, but excluded from aggregate precision, recall, and MRR.
